reason: Lateral veins 'not looped' / 'non réunies en arceaux' means the secondaries do not join in marginal loops, which is the negation of brochidodromous venation. As the earlier anastomosing note says, the quality belongs to the leaf or leaflet, not to the vein.
This is a part plus a measured dimension. The bearer is the petiole (the petiolule PO_0020050 for 'leaflet: stalks'), and the value is length (PATO_0000122) with a number and unit.
A compound of two apex/base shapes, rounded and almost truncate (truncated PATO_0000936, read as approximate). It is handled like 'linear-lanceolate', not as a new term.

label: semi-elliptic
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being half of an ellipse, bounded by a straight side along one axis of the ellipse and a curved side. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002232 semicircular.
reason: A standard outline term for sepals, indusia and lobes. PATO has semicircular but nothing for half an ellipse.
A climbing habit. 'High' only says how far it climbs and needs no term of its own.
A hyphenated spelling of the existing value class.
'Without midrib' / 'sans costa' states that the midrib is absent. midrib is an exact synonym of leaf midvein. 'Without distinct midrib' could instead be read as inconspicuous (PATO_0000464).
A pseudopedicel is a stalk-like narrowed base of the calyx or fruit above the true pedicel, so the part is borne on a stalk. That is what stipitate means.
A likeness whose meaning changes with the bearer: a knob-like short inflorescence shoot in one case, knobs on the calyx in another. Tuberculate surfaces already have FLOPO:0991060.
Scimitar-shaped means curved like a sabre or sickle. falciform has the synonyms falcate, sickle-shaped and scythe-shaped.
The part named (throat, lobe tips) is dark orange. The comparison with the rest of the corolla is dropped, and the part itself goes through docs/odp/12-part-of-qualified-whole.md.
A misspelling of lenticellate. The same rule as C204.
'Mouth' is a generic opening that needs its organ, like 'throat' and 'neck' in the previous review. 'Narrow' already has a term, and one example is a comparison ('narrower').
Unclear whether it means shape, size, fleshiness, colour or drupe type. Unlike cherry-like it has no agreed botanical reading, and there are only 4 statements.

label: scutiform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being broad, flattish and rounded in outline, like a small shield. NOTE: A shape, not an attachment; peltate (FLOPO:0991107) is the attachment of a stalk inside the margin.
reason: A recognised botanical shape term (scutiform) used for stipules, sepals, nectaries and filament bases. It must not be confused with peltate.
'Lower lip', 'lower bract', 'lower valve' give the position of the bearer in a series. They pick out the bearer and are not a quality of it.
Flecked means marked with small spots. Brown is the colour of the flecks, not of the bearer, so it cannot be added as a second value on the bearer.
A likeness to a part, applied to thorns, hairs and sheath outgrowths that are quite different things. There is no single quality to map to.
A strong smell is an odour of high intensity. This follows the previous mapping of 'tall' to increased height. The kind of smell (sweet, foetid) has its own FLOPO values.
Unclear: it can mean a base narrowed into a false petiole, a position just above the petiole, or 'almost petiolate'. Too few statements to settle which.
Wine-coloured (vinaceous) fruits and spadices are deep purplish red. dark red is the nearest existing colour, and reddish purple (PATO_0104079) is the other choice.
Stamens 'in bundles' are borne in close clusters from about the same point, which is fascicled. The number of bundles is a count (docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md).

label: isolateral
definition: A morphology quality inhering in a leaf by virtue of its mesophyll having palisade tissue on both the adaxial and the abaxial side, so that the two sides are alike in internal structure. NOTE: Botany-specific; opposite of dorsiventral (bifacial) leaf anatomy.
reason: A real leaf-anatomy term (eucalypts, xerophytes) with no PATO term. Bilateral symmetry is a different idea.
Antipetalous stamens stand opposite the petals. This is the relation opposite (PATO_0001933) towards petal (PO_0009032).
A ratio of width to height equal to 1 (approximate when the source has '±').

Autogamy is a mode of pollination (self-pollination), a process rather than a form of the flower. No existing PATO parent fits; phenotypic sex and closed do not. It is better kept as breeding-system trait data.
The margins carry a fringe of hairs, which is ciliate. 'Hairy' adds nothing here. 'Ciliées-villeuses' can also carry villous (FLOPO:0991051) as a second value.
A moss leaf term meaning both curled into a ring (circinate, PATO_0001964) and turned to one side (secund, FLOPO:0991146) at once. Both values apply together, so this is not a range between them.
A compound of two outlines, orbicular (PATO_0001934) and ovate (FLOPO:0991024), read like 'linear-lanceolate'.
In mosses, cirrate leaves are curled or coiled like tendrils when dry. 'Cirrate to crisped' sets it apart from crisped (FLOPO:0991148).
